Naomi / team — quick guidance from privacy side. High-level notes before we produce the artifacts: 

1) Subprocessors: we can share the current canonical list (see attached draft CSV). It includes subprocessors, purpose, country, and date of last access review. We should remove operational contact details (phone) for security.

2) TIA/DTIA scope: for a pilot that stores primarily Singapore and Australia data, our standard TIA covers transfers from APAC -> us-east (for control plane telemetry) and to EU when model variants are pulled. We must call out the fallback routing policy: model-serving fallback may route to 'hosted-europe' or 'hosted-us' depending on capacity — that's the main regulator question. I've attached a draft TIA workbook; note the rows where manual review is required (marked REVIEW).

3) UK addendum: the UK IDTA / addendum is only necessary if the customer sends personal data from the UK to Redwood or if they have UK-resident data subjects. If HealthBridge has UK users, we must offer the UK addendum signature. That said, the addendum doesn't change subprocessors but does require us to provide an evidence bundle (SCC+local supplement). Linda, can you confirm the latest text we should attach?

4) Evidence format: procurement tends to prefer a short 'evidence summary' PPT and a single zipped CSV + workbook. Proposal: produce one 2-slide PPT (summary + routing map) + subprocessors CSV + TIA workbook + link to SOC2 report (redacted) and our DPIA excerpt.

If the team is aligned, I'll mark items REVIEW and produce the attachments by 7/19 EOD.

- Karthik

Team / Simon — delivering the export bundle and next actions. Attached to this email (and uploaded to the Drive link below) are: 

- subprocessors_list_20280719.csv (redacted contacts, includes country + access justification)
- tia-scope-apac-draft.xlsx (marked REVIEW where legal input required)
- uk-addendum-diff.docx (short note on when the UK addendum applies + signature flow)
- evidence-summary-APAC-pilot.pptx (high-level two slides for procurement)

Quick highlights / routing flags:
- Primary data residency: Singapore (asia-sg-1) & Australia (asia-au-1).
- Control-plane telemetry may traverse us-east-1 for metrics; we have a minimal telemetry-only routing profile for pilot customers which we've documented in the TIA workbook.
- Model-serving fallback: in the event of capacity constraints we may route requests to hosted-eu-1 or hosted-us-1 depending on regional capacity policies. These fallbacks are documented in the 'Fallback routing' tab.
- UK addendum: applies only if HealthBridge processes UK-resident personal data. If applicable, procurement will need the signed addendum; legal (Linda) please confirm the final clause set in the attached diff.

Requested next actions: 
1) Simon / HealthBridge: confirm whether any UK-resident data subjects are in scope for the pilot (yes/no) and whether procurement needs the signed UK addendum at contract close.
2) Naomi: please provide the procurement contact and preferred DocuSign routing if they want the addendum signed.
3) Karthik / Linda: review TIA workbook rows marked REVIEW and provide final language by EOD 7/24.
4) Redwood Security: if there are any concerns with the control-plane telemetry note, flag immediately; otherwise we'll include the standard SOC2 link (redacted) in the final zip.

Simon, we tried to keep the pack concise for procurement intake. If you'd like a quick walk-through, I'm available for a 30-min sync early next week.

Thanks,
